verdicts.quote: Promotion is **automatic**: when a place frees, the first eligible waiting member is booked without a further confirmation step.
first accepted, first served … Two joins arriving together get distinct sequences, decided by the order the service commits them. … **Left out:** priority/tier ordering, manual reordering by staff.
**Left out (domain rules the request does not state):** waitlisting for several overlapping classes
verdicts.missing: There is no rule for what happens to the other overlapping entry when one class promotes the member.

verdicts.quote: a "decline this offer" step (G-4); penalties or fees for late cancellation (existing rule, preserved, unknown).
verdicts.missing: Automatic promotion has no decline step. The spec leaves open whether missing or cancelling an automatic booking counts under the existing penalty policy.

verdicts.quote: cancel(B) | **atomic:** B cancelled; first eligible waiting entry → promoted + booking created

informed they are now booked, class name and start … the in-app status changes … an outbound channel (email/push/SMS), the same message goes through it … notification delivery failure never reverses the promotion … the failure is logged
ana and ben cancel at the same time with W=[cy] … after both cancels cy is promoted exactly once, booked {cy}, count 1, one place free, W empty, I-1…I-5 hold
(book, cancel, join, leave, promote, capacity change, expiry) are serialised so that I-1…I-5 hold after each commit … a member has at most one of {booked booking, waiting entry} per class
Does promotion charge the member? | PD-7: reuse ordinary booking rules; skip ineligible
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves the timing of a charge open and does not say whether a failed charge skips the waiter, triggers a retry, or aborts the transaction.

verdicts.quote: The waitlist has **no product-imposed length cap**.
latest moment before start at which promotion is allowed (e.g. N minutes before) | Until start (PD-5)
verdicts.missing: The interim rule allows promotion right up to class start. The lead time for an earlier cutoff is unresolved.

verdicts.quote: the first (C′−booked) eligible waiting members are promoted, one place each, in order. … Lowering capacity below the current booked count keeps the existing rule of the app (unknown); it never creates or removes waiting entries.
staff cancels class with W=[cy,dee] → both `closed`, both informed

waitlist entries (member id, class id, sequence, status, timestamps) … monotonic per class, assigned at accept time … 1 + number of `waiting` entries with a smaller sequence. Derived, never stored independently

at the class start time every `waiting` entry becomes `expired` … Terminal entries are retained only for as long as and in the same manner as the existing app retains booking history for that class; no longer.
a member can read only their own waiting entry (status, position) and the **number** of people waiting on a class. They cannot read another member's identity, sequence or status.

verdicts.missing: The spec leaves staff roster access and removal open. It gives staff no action for manual promotion or view identifying who was promoted and when.
